module: Define the system and its compliance boundary

lesson.title: Identify the system, purpose and EU connection
lesson.summary: Identify the assessed system and its intended use before assigning duties.

blocks: This course follows **Northbridge Hiring**, a fictional supplier of candidate-ranking AI used by employers. The case facts are stipulated teaching facts. You will build a decision dossier: the evidence and reasons supporting a decision, with unresolved facts kept visible.

An **AI system** is machine-based, operates with some autonomy and infers from inputs how to produce predictions, content, recommendations or decisions for explicit or implicit objectives. Its outputs can influence physical or digital environments. It may adapt after deployment; adaptation is not compulsory.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(1), 2(10), 2(12), 3(1), 3(12); recital 12

blocks: **System boundary** means the functionality being assessed. A learned ranking service infers recommendations. A fixed rule that sorts dates, or a page displaying a stored article, does not establish AI status by itself.

Assess separate components and their combined operation. A conventional quiz displaying previously AI-written material is not automatically the same system as the AI authoring service. Human review does not remove the inference of that service.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(1), 2(10), 2(12), 3(1), 3(12); recital 12

blocks: **Intended purpose** is the use intended by the provider, including context and conditions, as specified in instructions, promotional or sales material, statements and technical documentation. A label such as “assistant” does not substitute for that evidence.

Northbridge advertises ranking job applicants to support shortlisting. Record the actual functions, users, inputs, outputs and decisions supported. Later changes to that purpose can change the applicable rules.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(1), 2(10), 2(12), 3(1), 3(12); recital 12

blocks: The **EU connection** can arise from placing a system on the Union market, EU-based deployment, or certain third-country activities where outputs are used in the Union. Record the actor and exact Article 2 connection; foreign hosting alone is not an exclusion.

Check exclusions on their terms. Purely personal non-professional use excludes deployer obligations, not every supplier duty. The free/open-source exclusion does not remove high-risk, Article 5 or Article 50 cases.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2(1), 2(10), 2(12), 3(1), 3(12); recital 12

blocks: First dossier entry: “Northbridge ranking service; intended to assist recruitment shortlisting; supplied to EU employers.” Keep the conventional document viewer separate.

For a real commercial product, unknown functionality or an unconfirmed EU connection remains a question to investigate. A confident product label is weaker evidence than the actual documented operation.
